issues.original: I designed and built this portfolio as a production-style Docusaurus documentation site to demonstrate documentation engineering, docs-as-code workflows, React/MDX customisation, automated QA, and CI/CD.
issues.message: The page states what was built and the technologies used, but does not establish the problem, constraint or opportunity the work addressed. The Challenge section lists tasks rather than a motivating problem, so a portfolio reader cannot see why the work mattered or what made it non-trivial.
issues.suggestion: Add a sentence in Context or Challenge describing the concrete problem or constraint the work addressed (for example, the need to demonstrate documentation-engineering capability, or a specific gap in existing tooling or workflow). Do not invent results; describe only the genuine motivation.

issues.original: For quality assurance, I wrote a Python script that combines the AI review with the deterministic checks such as link checking. The script validates the AI findings against the source to guard against hallucination, and generates a report containing the identified issues and suggested improvements.
issues.message: The hallucination-guarding validation is the most technically distinctive part of the work, but the page does not explain how the script validates AI findings against the source. A portfolio reader cannot assess the technical significance of this mechanism.
issues.suggestion: Add a brief description of the validation approach (for example, how findings are matched back to source text or what constitutes a validated versus rejected finding), without inventing implementation details that are not true.

issues.original: This portfolio demonstrates a modern docs-as-code workflow, reusable documentation components, and automated deployment and quality checks.
issues.message: The Impact section restates the deliverables rather than describing any outcome, adoption or observable result. It does not distinguish impact from the Implementation section.
issues.suggestion: Either describe genuine outcomes (for example, how the QA pipeline or taxonomy machinery is used, maintained or extended) or reframe the section to state what the work demonstrates about the author's capability, avoiding fabricated metrics.

issues.original: The first phase of the Developer Center soft-launched in December 2016 during a period of rapid growth and change at Paysafe. The company reported 2016 revenue of just over $1 billion while continuing to integrate the Skrill and Optimal Payments businesses.
issues.message: The revenue and business-integration context is company-level background rather than evidence of the documentation work's impact. As written, the Impact section leads with corporate financials before establishing what the documentation work achieved, which can dilute the portfolio reader's understanding of the author's contribution.
issues.suggestion: Lead the Impact section with the documentation outcome (e.g. the soft launch and what it consolidated or enabled for developers), and keep the company context brief and clearly subordinate to that outcome.

issues.original: At Morgan Stanley, I led the design, launch and evolution of a custom internal docs-as-code platform and developer portal, alongside my work as lead technical writer for the Optimus and RICE frameworks.
issues.message: The page devotes substantial space (lines 67-77) to explaining the Optimus and RICE product technology, but the case study's principal deliverable is the documentation platform. The product description is longer than the description of the platform's own architecture and design decisions, which dilutes the documentation-engineering focus.
issues.suggestion: Consider condensing the 'Documentation content' subsection to a brief framing of what Optimus and RICE are and why their documentation was complex, and redirect the freed space to the platform's architecture, design decisions or governance model.

issues.original: I owned platform direction, requirements, testing and quality, working with a dedicated engineering team on the initial implementation. I later contributed directly to the codebase, extending functionality and resolving issues as adoption grew.
issues.message: The split of ownership between the author and the engineering team is stated but not made concrete: it is unclear which parts of the platform the author personally designed or built versus directed. This makes it harder for a portfolio reader to assess the author's hands-on contribution.
issues.suggestion: Clarify the boundary of personal ownership, for example which components the author specified, designed, tested or implemented directly, and which were delivered by the engineering team under the author's direction.

issues.original: I designed the search approach for a growing documentation set, combining fast, keyword-based JavaScript client-side search with the slower corporate RAG-based search for more complex natural-language queries. I also tested search behaviour and retrieval quality; the engineering team implemented the production solution.
issues.message: The search work is described at a high level, but the design rationale and the testing/validation approach are not evidenced. A portfolio reader cannot see what made the hybrid search design non-trivial or how retrieval quality was validated.
issues.suggestion: Add brief detail on the design trade-offs (for example why client-side keyword search was combined with RAG rather than a single approach) and on how search behaviour and retrieval quality were tested, such as the kinds of queries or evaluation method used.

issues.original: A major contribution was my proposal to serve the generated documentation from an attached filesystem instead of copying the content into the container, reducing build time by approximately **15 minutes**.
issues.message: The 15-minute build-time reduction is stated without a baseline, so its significance is hard to judge. A reader cannot tell whether this is a large or small proportional improvement.
issues.suggestion: State the baseline build time or the proportional reduction so the impact of the change is clear.

issues.original: I wrote the user documentation for version 5 of AMX Composer, a content-management application for the AMX Digital Signage platform. Version 5 was a complete rewrite of the original Windows client-server application with many new features including a redesigned user interface, and a new web-based technology stack.
issues.message: The page spends a substantial portion of its opening on describing the underlying product and its rewrite rather than the documentation work. The product description is useful context, but the balance leans toward explaining the technology rather than the author's documentation contribution.
issues.suggestion: Consider trimming the product/rewrite description to the minimum needed for context and foregrounding the documentation scope (audiences, outputs, single-sourcing) earlier.

issues.original: The HTML help and PDF manual were successfully released with the product and received positive internal feedback from the developers and product manager.
issues.message: The outcome is asserted but not evidenced. A portfolio reader cannot gauge the scale or significance of the work from 'positive internal feedback' alone.
issues.suggestion: Where available, add concrete evidence of scale or impact (for example approximate page/topic counts, number of help bundles, or the scope of content covered) rather than inventing metrics.

issues.original: I worked with another technical writer to advocate for a docs-as-code alternative. Together, we specified the requirements for the first version of the new platform and tested early prototypes.
issues.message: The docs-as-code platform work is a significant documentation-engineering contribution, but the page does not clarify the author's specific ownership versus the other writer's, nor the scale or impact of the platform. A portfolio reader cannot easily distinguish the author's individual contribution from the joint effort.
issues.suggestion: Clarify what the author personally owned (for example, which requirements, which prototype testing, or which aspects of the specification) and, if known, the scope of the platform's adoption.

issues.original: I built working test integrations for the supported Masterpass flows to validate the documented procedures against actual API behaviour.
issues.message: The testing work is described but the page does not convey the technical substance of the test integrations (for example, how they were built, what tooling was used, or what kinds of discrepancies were found). This weakens the evidence for a documentation-validation contribution.
issues.suggestion: Add brief detail on how the test integrations were constructed and the nature of the discrepancies uncovered, without inventing specifics.

issues.original: After completing the guide, I also helped recommend and test an early version of Mastercard's replacement docs-as-code authoring system. Mastercard subsequently adopted docs-as-code for its Developer Center.
issues.message: This docs-as-code contribution is a significant documentation-engineering deliverable but is described only in passing, with no detail on what was recommended, what was tested, or the author's specific role. A portfolio reader cannot assess the nature or scale of this contribution.
issues.suggestion: Expand this into its own short subsection describing what the author personally evaluated or tested, the criteria or problems it addressed, and the outcome, so the documentation-engineering contribution is legible.

issues.original: Once I had working integrations, I tested the API workflows and checked the OpenAPI-based reference documentation. I subsequently worked with the product owner to correct these errors and omissions in the OpenAPI definitions.
issues.message: The page states that errors and omissions were found and corrected but gives no concrete example of the kind of defect discovered. Concrete examples would substantiate the validation work and demonstrate its value.
issues.suggestion: Add one or two brief, non-sensitive examples of the types of errors or omissions found in the OpenAPI reference (for example, incorrect field descriptions, missing parameters or wrong example values) to evidence the validation work.

issues.original: I tested the documented workflow against the Paysafe.js implementation, with input from product and engineering teams to ensure that the instructions and examples reflected the expected behaviour.
issues.message: The page mentions testing the documented workflow but does not describe how it was validated or what evidence resulted. For a documentation-engineering portfolio, the validation approach is a meaningful part of the contribution and is currently underspecified.
issues.suggestion: Briefly describe the validation approach (for example, whether examples were run against a sandbox, what was checked, or how regressions were caught) so the reader can assess the rigour of the documentation validation.

issues.original: The guide gave developers a practical route from understanding Paysafe.js and its compliance benefits to completing a working browser-based payment-tokenisation integration.
issues.message: The Outcome section restates the guide's purpose rather than reporting any observable result. A portfolio reader cannot tell whether the guide was adopted, reduced support burden, or otherwise had an effect.
issues.suggestion: If available, add a concrete outcome such as adoption, developer feedback, reduction in integration questions, or reuse of the CodePen/Try Now pattern. If no outcome data exists, state that explicitly rather than implying impact.

issues.original: I designed and implemented a governed taxonomy for a Docusaurus documentation site. The project combined information architecture, docs-as-code automation, editor integration, and AI-assisted classification.
issues.message: The opening frames the deliverable as a taxonomy for a Docusaurus site but does not state the scale or context of the corpus (for example, that it governs a portfolio of case studies and implementation guides). A portfolio reader cannot gauge the scope of the work from the page alone.
issues.suggestion: Add a brief, factual statement of the corpus the taxonomy governs (for example, the number and kinds of documents) so the reader can understand the scale of the governance problem.

issues.original: I implemented the taxonomy schema, validation and migration tooling, AI review workflow, and editor integration to make it easy for writers to select appropriate tags from controlled metadata when tagging their documents.
issues.message: The page establishes what was built but does not identify who the writers are or what problem they faced before the system existed. Without that, the value of the editor integration and review workflow is harder to assess.
issues.suggestion: Add a short statement of the intended users (for example, the author as sole writer, or a team of contributors) and the prior pain point the system addressed.

issues.original: In the historical correction-migration example, five vocabulary changes were validated against 26 portfolio documents, and no document rewrites were required because the canonical IDs did not change. The current add-only migration path does not scan unrelated documents.
issues.message: The only quantified outcome is explicitly historical and is immediately qualified as not reflecting current behaviour, so the page provides no evidence of the current system's effect. A portfolio reader is left without a concrete measure of the delivered system.
issues.suggestion: Add a factual outcome for the current workflow, such as the size of the canonical vocabulary, the number of governed documents, or the number of migrations applied, if such figures are available.

issues.original: Performed hands-on technical troubleshooting during the migration, such as suggesting a way to save 15 minutes on each documentation build, and personally resolved most of the minor post-deployment issues
issues.message: The '15 minutes saved per build' detail is the only quantified outcome on the page, but it is framed as a suggestion rather than a delivered result, and the sentence mixes a minor optimisation with post-deployment issue resolution. A portfolio reader cannot tell what was actually implemented or what the aggregate impact was.
issues.suggestion: Clarify whether the build-time saving was implemented and, if so, state the resulting impact (for example, the effect on build frequency or contributor turnaround). Consider separating the build optimisation from the post-deployment troubleshooting so each contribution is legible.

issues.original: Built an automated release-note generation workflow by integrating structured Jira issue data into documentation processes.
issues.message: The automation section describes the workflow's inputs but not what it produces or who benefits, so the documentation-engineering value is hard to assess. The reader cannot tell whether release notes were generated, published, or merely drafted.
issues.suggestion: Add a brief statement of the workflow's output and its consumers (for example, generated release notes published to the portal for a named audience), and note the author's ownership of the implementation.

issues.original: * Using cURL to test endpoints from the command line.
issues.message: Trailing whitespace after the sentence, and this bullet ends with a full stop while the surrounding bullets do not, producing inconsistent list punctuation.
issues.suggestion: Remove the trailing space and the terminal full stop so the bullet matches the others: '* Using cURL to test endpoints from the command line'

issues.original: I have modified existing MkDocs plugins where required. I also led and specified the requirements for a custom static-site generator, contributed to its technical design, carried out all the user testing, and later worked directly on its development.
issues.message: The custom static-site generator work is described here in general terms, and the same project is described again at line 213 with more specific ownership detail. The two passages overlap without cross-referencing, which can make a portfolio reader unsure whether they describe the same platform or two different ones.
issues.suggestion: Add a brief cross-reference (for example, 'the Morgan Stanley developer-documentation platform described below') or consolidate the ownership description so the reader can tell the two passages refer to the same work.

issues.original: At Morgan Stanley, I led the design and evolution of a large-scale internal docs-as-code platform and developer portal supporting an API platform with a large internal developer audience.
issues.message: The scale of the platform and audience is described only in vague terms ("large-scale", "large internal developer audience"). For a principal-level case study, this leaves the reader unable to gauge the significance of the work, and the page elsewhere does provide a concrete page-count metric, so the vagueness here is inconsistent.
issues.suggestion: Where the information is available, quantify the platform scale and audience (for example, number of internal developers served or number of APIs documented) to make the significance of the deliverable concrete.

issues.original: I owned product direction, requirements, solution design, testing, quality, and feature prioritisation. I initially worked with a dedicated engineering team on implementation and later contributed directly to the codebase as the platform evolved.
issues.message: The page states that the author contributed directly to the codebase but does not indicate the nature or extent of that engineering contribution, which is a key piece of documentation-engineering evidence for a principal-level portfolio.
issues.suggestion: Add a brief indication of what the direct codebase contribution involved (for example, the kinds of components, tooling or automation implemented) so the engineering contribution is legible to a portfolio reader.

issues.original: I have several years of experience creating and maintaining software architecture-governance documentation for complex financial systems. My work combined accurate meeting records, architecture diagrams, action tracking, metadata governance and workflow automation.
issues.message: The page opens with a general experience summary but does not establish the problem, constraint or opportunity the governance work addressed, nor the scale or nature of the documentation estate. A portfolio reader cannot tell why this work mattered or what made it difficult.
issues.suggestion: Add a short framing sentence describing the governance problem or context (for example, the size or complexity of the estate, the compliance or consistency risk being managed, or the stakeholders served) so the value of the work is clear before the bullet lists.

issues.original: I built a documentation-platform plugin for embedding C4 architecture diagrams in Markdown. Diagram definitions were stored as text alongside the supporting documentation, allowing diagrams and content to be version-controlled, reviewed and audited together.
issues.message: This is the strongest documentation-engineering contribution on the page, but it is described in only two sentences with no indication of the platform, the implementation approach, or the outcome. The reader cannot assess the technical significance or the author's ownership beyond 'I built'.
issues.suggestion: Expand this section to state the platform the plugin targeted, the approach taken (for example, how diagram definitions were parsed and rendered), and any evidence of use or outcome, without inventing details not available.

issues.original: A pilot using an approved internal Whisper speech-to-text model to generate draft transcripts from meeting recordings for human review and correction.
issues.message: The automation bullets describe activities but not their effect. The reader cannot tell whether these automations reduced effort, improved accuracy or were adopted, which weakens the evidence of operational value.
issues.suggestion: Where genuine information exists, add a brief note on the outcome or adoption of these automations (for example, time saved, error reduction or whether the pilot progressed), without fabricating metrics.

issues.original: Redesigning the information architecture for approximately 500 pages for the new developer documentation site at Morgan Stanley, replacing a flat collection of loosely connected pages with a structured content hierarchy and clearer navigation paths that improved discoverability and content organisation.
issues.message: The claim that the redesign 'improved discoverability and content organisation' is asserted without any supporting evidence (metrics, before/after comparison, or validation method). A portfolio reader cannot distinguish a measured outcome from an expectation, which weakens the credibility of the strongest IA example on the page.
issues.suggestion: Either qualify the outcome as an intended/observed result without measurement, or add the kind of evidence that would substantiate it (e.g. analytics, search-success or navigation metrics, or a stated validation approach).

issues.original: Designing the information architecture supporting a RAG-based documentation search system, including generation of a comprehensive site map and analysis of retrieval issues affecting search relevance and answer quality.
issues.message: This entry and the metadata entry on line 53 both concern RAG-based documentation search, but the page does not make clear whether they are the same initiative or separate pieces of work, nor what the author personally produced versus analysed. The relationship between the two is ambiguous for a portfolio reader assessing scope and ownership.
issues.suggestion: Clarify whether these are one initiative or two, and state the concrete artefact or change the author owned (e.g. the site map, the metadata schema, the retrieval-issue analysis) so the contribution is unambiguous.

issues.original: Built a personal Kubernetes cluster on Proxmox.
issues.message: The Kubernetes item is a personal/homelab activity with no stated documentation or documentation-engineering relevance, and it sits alongside professional deliverables without distinguishing the two. A portfolio reader cannot tell what this demonstrates about documentation work.
issues.suggestion: Either connect this to a documentation-relevant outcome (for example, what was run or validated on the cluster in service of documentation) or clearly frame it as personal learning so its status is unambiguous.

issues.original: Proposed serving the generated documentation from an attached file system instead, reducing build time by approximately **15 minutes**.
issues.message: The 15-minute build-time reduction is a strong, concrete result but the page does not state the baseline build time, so the reader cannot gauge the relative magnitude of the improvement.
issues.suggestion: Add the original build time (or the percentage reduction) so the 15-minute saving can be interpreted.

issues.original: Advanced experience with **Graphviz/DOT**, including developing an internal Graphviz-based tool at Morgan Stanley that generated hyperlinked **trail diagrams**. These diagrams provided structured learning paths through related developer documentation, improving the site navigation.
issues.message: This is the strongest documentation-engineering evidence on the page (building an internal tool that generated navigation diagrams), but it is compressed into a single bullet with no indication of the problem it solved, who used it, or the author's ownership beyond 'developing'. A portfolio reader cannot gauge the scale or significance of the contribution.
issues.suggestion: Expand this into a short case-study passage stating the navigation problem it addressed, who the users were (e.g. developers navigating the documentation site), what the author personally designed and built, and any available evidence of outcome. Do not invent metrics; describe only what actually happened.

issues.original: Experienced maintaining large diagram sets including using **OCR to identify outdated terminology** to fix in screenshots and other bitmap/raster-based diagrams.
issues.message: The OCR-based maintenance workflow is a distinctive documentation-engineering practice, but it is presented as a bare capability claim with no context on the problem (stale terminology across large bitmap diagram sets) or how the workflow operated. Its value as portfolio evidence is therefore hard to assess.
issues.suggestion: Briefly describe the maintenance problem, how the OCR workflow was applied, and what it achieved (e.g. detecting and correcting outdated labels at scale). Avoid inventing specifics not supported by the source.

issues.original: Used **MkDocs and a number of plugins** to recreate functionality from a large internal Wiki documentation site as a pilot project.
issues.message: The MkDocs work is described only as a pilot with no stated outcome, so a portfolio reader cannot tell whether the recreation succeeded, what was validated, or what the pilot demonstrated. The value of the documentation-engineering contribution is therefore unclear.
issues.suggestion: Add the result or purpose of the pilot, for example what was proven (feasibility of migration, parity with the Wiki, performance at scale) and any outcome that is factually available.

issues.original: Recompiled the modified plugins as standalone executables for deployment.
issues.message: The reason for recompiling plugins as standalone executables is not explained, so the reader cannot see what constraint or deployment problem this solved. Without that, the technical significance of the step is unclear.
issues.suggestion: State the constraint that required standalone executables (for example the deployment environment or plugin packaging limitations) and what this enabled.

issues.original: Defined and tested fast client-side documentation search using FlexSearch, alongside integrating the slower central search service for broader queries.
issues.message: The search work is asserted but no evidence or outcome is referenced, so the reader cannot judge the scale or effectiveness of the integration. The comparative claim about speed is also unsupported in the text.
issues.suggestion: Reference available evidence such as the live implementation, index size, page counts searched, or measured behaviour, and clarify the division of labour between client-side and central search.

issues.original: Tested RAG-based retrieval, including indexing, sitemap generation and proposed metadata changes to improve retrieval relevance.
issues.message: This bullet mixes testing, indexing, sitemap generation and a proposal without indicating what was personally owned versus proposed, which slightly blurs the author's contribution.
issues.suggestion: Separate what was implemented and tested from what was proposed, so the reader can distinguish delivered work from recommendations.

issues.original: I applied these capabilities to the automation, integration and migration projects described in the [Flare Automation, Integration and Migration](#automation) section.
issues.message: This sentence is a forward reference to a section that appears later on the same page. It adds little and slightly interrupts the flow between the skills grids and the concrete evidence that follows.
issues.suggestion: Consider removing this sentence, or moving it to the end of the page as a summary pointer, so the reader reaches the concrete evidence (user documentation, community contributions, automation projects) without a detour.

issues.original: At Paysafe, I integrated Flare with development, publishing and review systems as part of a broader documentation tool chain used to manage all the non-API-reference documentation on the launch version of the [Paysafe Developer Centre](https://developer.paysafe.com).
issues.message: The page establishes the tool chain and the systems integrated, but does not state the outcome or value of the automation and migration work (for example, what the review workflow or migration enabled that was not possible before). This is the kind of context that would strengthen the portfolio evidence.
issues.suggestion: Add a brief statement of the outcome or benefit of the automation, integration and migration work, such as the scale of content migrated, the review turnaround or the maintenance burden reduced, using only facts you can substantiate.

issues.original: * Maintained **Swagger 2.0 / OpenAPI 2.0 specifications** at Mastercard covering HTTP methods, status codes, headers, query string & path parameters, request and response bodies, and authentication mechanisms, supporting automated generation of API reference documentation. Used similar technology, API Blueprint, at Paysafe.
issues.message: The page lists tools and activities but does not establish the scale, scope or outcome of the specification work (for example, how many APIs or specifications, which teams or products depended on the generated reference, or what improved as a result). Without this, a portfolio reader cannot gauge the significance of the contribution.
issues.suggestion: Add concrete scope or outcome context where it is genuinely available, such as the number or scale of specifications maintained, the consumers of the generated reference documentation, or a measurable improvement in consistency or maintenance effort.

issues.original: Reviewed API contracts against implemented REST behaviour, identifying discrepancies in parameters, schemas, status codes, authentication and API responses, and working with engineers to resolve issues and update the specification and documentation.
issues.message: The validation work is described as an activity but the page does not indicate whether it was systematic or repeatable (for example, a defined review process, test harness or workflow) versus ad hoc. This affects how a reader assesses the documentation-engineering maturity of the contribution.
issues.suggestion: Clarify whether the contract-review and validation work followed a repeatable process, tooling or workflow, and what it produced (for example, corrected specifications, regression prevention or a documented validation approach).

issues.original: I have nearly five years of C/C++ software engineering experience; this includes work in 2D/3D graphics, GIS, CAD/VR systems, and graphics device drivers at STMicroelectronics. Additionally, I developed cross-platform C code for Windows and Unix, to modify and extend a 3D CAD application. In later roles, I worked with STL containers and data structures for application logic and data processing. My C# experience includes developing tooling to automate the generation of release-notes from tagged JIRA tickets using the JIRA REST API, inserting the retrieved data into MadCap Flare XHTML templates to produce the final document.
issues.message: This section is a dense prose paragraph while every other section uses bulleted lists, and it mixes two distinct things: general C/C++ software-engineering background (largely unrelated to documentation work) and a genuinely relevant documentation-engineering deliverable (the JIRA-to-Flare release-notes automation). The relevant documentation tooling is buried at the end of a paragraph dominated by non-documentation engineering history.
issues.suggestion: Split into bullets and lead with the documentation-relevant work, e.g. a bullet for the C# JIRA REST API to MadCap Flare release-notes automation, then separate bullets for the C/C++ background. This keeps the page focused on documentation-engineering evidence rather than general software history.

issues.original: I implemented the pipeline in [`scripts/ai_docs_review.py`](scripts/ai_docs_review.py). It combines AI-assisted editorial review with deterministic checks and established documentation tools, producing both HTML and JSON reports.
issues.message: The README describes the QA pipeline's capabilities in detail but does not state the problem it addressed, the users it serves, or why the work was valuable. For a portfolio case study, this context helps a reader understand the significance of the engineering contribution rather than just its feature list.
issues.suggestion: Add a short paragraph explaining the problem the pipeline solved (for example, the risk of unverified AI findings or inconsistent documentation quality), who benefits from it (contributors, maintainers, readers), and what outcome it enables. Do not invent specifics; describe only what is true of the project.

issues.original: Led the documentation work for the first Paysafe Developer Center during a period of exceptional expansion as the company delivered 21% organic revenue growth, and surpassed $1 billion in annual revenue for the first time.
issues.message: The company-level revenue metrics are not clearly tied to the documentation work, so a portfolio reader may read them as borrowed business context rather than evidence of the author's contribution. The card also says less about what was actually delivered than the first case study card.
issues.suggestion: Keep any company context brief and add a concrete statement of what was delivered or materially improved (for example the developer centre's structure, API reference, or publishing approach) so the card demonstrates the documentation contribution rather than the company's financial results.
